sections.title: Situation
sections.prompt: What is the board really asking for, and which numbers show the size of the problem?
criteria: Restates the ask as testable outcomes for month 6: inventory with owners, high-risk assessments evidenced, board oversight
Counts the work due by month 6 (306 items) including the queue and new proposals, not just the 212 in production
Shows that a full assessment for every item (36,720 h) and even a tiered central-only approach (5,211 h vs 4,680 h) do not fit
Puts a number on what the queue costs (about €3.17M of claims savings per month of delay)

sections.title: Stakeholders
sections.prompt: Who has a stake, what does each want, and how do you bring them along?
criteria: Covers the board risk committee, the supervisor, the CRO, the CFO and the country CEOs, each with a distinct want
Separates the 3 countries with data science teams from the other 6
Offers the countries something concrete for registering systems, such as an amnesty or a service level
Ends with one idea that ties the stakeholders together

sections.title: Options
sections.prompt: What operating models are possible, and how does each fare against the supervisor's tests and the hours?
criteria: Compares at least central, federated and hub-and-spoke on one table, plus a freeze or do-nothing option
Computes hours against capacity for each option rather than asserting fit
Shows that a federated model fails the independence test the supervisor will apply
Gives a three-year cost for each option

sections.title: Decision and Trade-offs
sections.prompt: What do you recommend, what do you give up, and what would make you change it?
criteria: Makes one recommendation with tiers and a country-level first line
Keeps approval of high-risk systems away from the people who build them, including the candidate's own platform
Says the decision is reversible per country and how
Gives measurable triggers, such as a sampling defect rate or a service-level breach

sections.title: Economics
sections.prompt: What does each option cost over three years, and what does delay cost?
criteria: Compares three-year totals and separates new spend from people already on payroll
Shows year-one new spend (€1.22M) against the €1.5M cap
Prices the claims programme delay and labels the assumption behind it
Names the opportunity cost of the country leads' time

sections.title: Org and Ownership
sections.prompt: Who is accountable, who approves, and who does the work in each line?
criteria: Names one accountable executive
Places the approval body and the central reviewers in the second line under the CRO
Requires a named business owner for every inventory entry
Includes internal audit as the third line with a dated review

sections.title: Plan and Milestones
sections.prompt: What happens between now and the supervisor's review, and where can you still correct course?
criteria: Completes all high-risk assessments before month 6
Clears the claims programme's queued assessments early, not after the high-risk work
Has at least one gate with a measurable threshold
Runs a mock review or internal audit dry run before month 6

sections.title: Risk and Governance
sections.prompt: What could undermine the model, and what controls produce evidence a supervisor can test?
criteria: Treats unregistered systems as the main risk and has a technical control for it, such as gateway keys tied to an inventory id
Samples first-line assessments with a stated rate and a consequence for failure
Has a fallback if the high-risk underwriting model fails its assessment
Uses frameworks such as NIST AI RMF or ISO/IEC 42001 as structure without making certification a month-6 goal

sections.title: Metrics
sections.prompt: How do you know the model works, and what would show it is being gamed?
criteria: Pairs each success metric with a guard metric
Tracks review time by tier against a stated service level
Tracks unregistered systems found after the amnesty
Avoids activity metrics such as number of policies or trainings

sections.title: Communication
sections.prompt: What does each audience hear, and how often?
criteria: Gives a one-line message for at least four audiences, including the supervisor and the country CEOs
Tells the CFO new spend and existing people separately
Sets a cadence to the board until the review and after it
Reports failed gates and sampling defects as well as progress
